messages:
maria: FYI CI started failing for edge-sdk tests after we flipped packages to ESM-only. Jest jobs error with "Cannot use import statement outside a module" when loading __mocks__ files.

rachel: hmm that sounds like our runner still treating mock files as CJS. Which mock is blowing up?

maria: __mocks__/node-fetch.ts (we re-export from an ESM-only http lib). Log:```
TypeError [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: Must use import to load ES Module: /workspace/node_modules/esm-http-lib/index.mjs
```

dan: Are we running root-level jest which defaults to CJS? We have a few packages with "type":"module" but root is still CJS. That mismatch is the classic footgun.

oliver: For Vitest I noticed similar but Vitest runs under ESM and only fails when mocks are hoisted before esbuild transpile. Setting deps.inline for the internal package fixes it:```
// vitest.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ test: { deps: { inline: ['@redwood/edge-sdk'] } } })
```

rachel: Could we just convert __mocks__ to use dynamic import so both runners are happy? e.g.```
// __mocks__/node-fetch.ts
let real;
beforeAll(async () => { real = await import('../../src/node-fetch'); });
export const fetch = vi.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ ok: true }));
```

dan: dynamic import works for Vitest but not for Jest CJS mocks which are loaded synchronously. Also Jest's manual mocks expect module.exports.

maria: I prototyped two approaches locally:
1) Per-package ESM Jest runner using ts-jest with "useESM": true and package.json "type":"module". Pros: keeps tests ESM-native. Cons: ts-jest + monorepo paths caused sourcemap offsets and slow startup.
2) Keep Jest as CJS and compile problematic mocks to CJS pretest (small Babel/tsc step for __mocks__). Pros: minimal change. Cons: build step is hacky and slower.

oliver: Another option: run edge-suite under Vitest in CI only (split job). That way production runner is still Jest for other packages. We can gate it behind a 2-week experiment.

rachel: Any typing complaints? TS errors in tests?

maria: Yep. TS complains about default vs named exports when we mock modules that only export ESM default. Workaround was to enable "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true in tsconfig.test or cast with `as unknown as typeof import('module')` in mocks. Not pretty.

dan: Action items I propose:
- Short term: Add CI job that runs edge-sdk tests with Vitest (native ESM) so PRs catch breakages.
- Medium: Document canonical mock patterns for Jest(CJS), Jest(ESM), and Vitest in devex docs.
- Long term: decide whether monorepo moves to ESM root or maintain mixed-mode and standardize per-package test runners.

oliver: I've opened a small PR converting one failing test to Vitest to prove the approach: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-sdk/pull/728. It includes vitest config, deps.inline, and snapshot migration notes.

ci-bot: CI: workflow #5130 failed on job jest-edge (see https://ci.internal/runs/5130)

test-bot: Note: created ticket INF-1035 to track "edge-sdk test ESM/CJS mock compatibility" and assigned to @maria.

rachel: Thanks. If we go Vitest route I'll help port helpers and snapshot storage.

maria: I'll add a short doc in docs/devex with examples and open a follow-up to add the temporary Vitest CI job. Will reference INF-1035.

dan: ping me for any ts-jest tuning if we decide to keep Jest ESM.

oliver: Also add troubleshooting blurb about sourcemap line offsets when using ts-jest + useESM. Saved me an hour. :sweat_smile:

maria: cool. I'll post a summary and link to the PR in INF-1035. Thanks all.
